alignments.note: The ASV writes only "for" here, which answers to γάρ; no English word realizes the connective καί, so it is its own unrepresented unit under rule 23.
The genitive pronoun ἡμῶν is present and free to carry the possessive "our", so rule 20 proper applies and the article realizes nothing.
θεός → "God", bare, the determiner slot being taken by the possessive on ἡμῶν.

Verbless clause with an expressed noun subject (ὁ θεός), so rule 63 gives the supplied copula to the predicate nominal rather than to the subject: πῦρ takes "is a … fire", discontinuously under rule 15, exactly as πνεῦμα ὁ θεός → "God is a Spirit" does. Headed on "fire", the word realizing the lexeme.
Attributive participle καταναλίσκον → "consuming", split from its noun under rule 26.

review_notes: All 7 source and 7 target ids partitioned exactly once.
καί is left unrepresented: the ASV's single "for" answers to γάρ, and no second connective word is written. A reference comparison may report this as a disagreement.
The copula placement follows rule 63 (noun subject → predicate nominal carries "is"), not the ASV's word order, which writes "God is" together.
